messages:
maria-support: FYI - Acme Insights payment (INV-8721) just bounced. payments-bot forwarded the return with reason 'Invalid IBAN checksum'. Details below, assigning to finance to advise next steps.

payments-bot: ALERT: Wire return received for payment_id=pay_01G2X9HB. Return reason: "INVALID_IBAN_CHECKSUM". Originating bank: First Republic, beneficiary bank: DEUTDEFFXXX, raw beneficiary_iban=DE89 3704 0044 0532 0130 00 (as provided). Returned amount: $45,210. Invoice: INV-8721.

maria-support: Customer says they copied IBAN from billing portal. They need this resolved today — told them we're investigating. @aj-finance can you confirm whether we should request corrected IBAN from the customer or reissue as ACH?

aj-finance: On it. Two quick checks: 1) Did our system store any non-numeric characters/spaces? 2) Is this a SEPA wire or domestic? Looks like beneficiary IBAN -> SEPA (DE). If checksum invalid we should ask customer to confirm full IBAN (no spaces) and ask their bank for the correct formatted IBAN. We can hold funds and resubmit once corrected.

sophie-cs: Customer says their treasury confirmed IBAN was provided by their bank. They asked if we can try re-submitting — they prefer not to reissue via ACH.

lin-eng: I pulled the payment log; our wire payload shows beneficiary_iban="DE89 3704 0044 0532 0130 00" with spaces. Our payment-sender service strips spaces before submission normally, but I see an odd path where draft invoices submitted via the billing UI didn't run normalization. Code path: billing-ui -> invoice-service -> payments-micro. Will open a ticket.

remy-ops: For immediate unblocking we can manually normalize and resubmit the wire from our portal, but ops needs written confirmation from customer to reattempt. Also flagging for audit: need to redact account numbers in logs.

aj-finance: Proposed plan: 1) Ask customer to confirm IBAN (no spaces), or provide a new payment instruction from their bank. 2) If they confirm, ops can attempt a re-submit today (manual) and we can mark invoice as 'reattempting' so accounting knows. 3) If they want faster resolution and are OK with ACH (not ideal for DE), offer refund and ACH/alternative.

maria-support: I messaged Acme with the ask (copying the exact string we need): 
```
Please confirm the beneficiary IBAN exactly as issued by your bank with no spaces or punctuation, and confirm the beneficiary bank SWIFT/BIC. Example format: DE89370400440532013000
We need written authorization to attempt a manual resubmission.
```

sophie-cs: They replied: "Thanks, that was a typo on our side — missing a digit at the end. Correct IBAN is DE89370400440532013001. We'll authorize re-submit now."

aj-finance: Great. Remy, pls proceed with manual normalization + resubmit once you have customer auth. Keep payment_id same for trace. Also record return reason and remedy in the invoice notes.

remy-ops: Will do. I scrubbed the logs and added a redaction rule to hide IBAN patterns in plain text (and raised infra ticket #INF-922 to enforce normalization in the billing UI). ETA for manual retry: 90 minutes after auth.

lin-eng: Opening PR to ensure billing-ui normalizes/validates IBAN fields on submit; will include a client-side checksum check (IBAN modulus) and server-side validation. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/billing-ui/pull/458

maria-support: Closing loop with customer: told them ops will retry and we'll update here when confirmed. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

payments-bot: UPDATE: Manual resubmit succeeded, settlement initiated. New payment_id=pay_01G2Y7KF. Final status: SENT to bank. Invoice INV-8721 marked paid pending settlement.

maria-support: Marking this thread resolved after settlement clears. Capturing follow-ups: billing-ui validation, infra redaction, and add a line to our payment-runbook for IBAN checksum errors.
